newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Thames TV wants stake in Portugal's TVI - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thames TV wants stake in Portugal's TVI - paper.

text.p: Britain's Thames Television is interested in taking a strategic stake in private Portuguese TV channel Televisao Independente (TVI), the daily Publico reported.
Publico said the president of the Portuguese channel, Carlos Monjardino, had confirmed that a British company had made a written proposal but he declined to give the name.
Thames Television is part of Britain's Pearson Plc media group, publisher of the Financial Times.
No TVI officials were available to comment on the report on Friday, a public holiday in Portugal.
Publico said negotiations between TVI and Scandinavian Broadcasting System (SBS) together with the Portuguese Soci group had stalled over disagreements about the channel's financial restructuring.
Monjardino told the paper the disagreements were not fundamental.
According to Publico, SBS and Soci planned to invest 1.5 billion escudos ($9.8 million) in TVI which would give them a 20 percent stake.
Monjardino said he had made a trip to London last month to hold discussions with the channel's majority shareholders who are London-based funds.
He said TVI planned to hold a general assembly by the end of the year.
